Really wish I would have given this game a shot sooner.  The campaign is very meh, but the multiplayer versus and horde modes are surprisingly good.  

Even for its age, the graphics aren't terrible.  And I was surprised to find that there are still enough people playing online to find a versus or exterminatus (horde) match.  If you're a 40k lover, and you're interested in Gears of War style gameplay, there is plenty of fun to be had with this game. The progression system is addicting as you unlock new weapons, skills, and better looking armor.  In multiplayer versus mode, the game maintains balance by allowing you to copy the loadout of whoever killed you for your next death.  This is very useful and keeps you from feeling like you'll never be able to get kills or level up.  The game also does a pretty good job of maintaining balance between the different classes and weapons.  In a populated match with a decent connection, 

All of that said, it's not perfect.  There are no dedicated servers, so it can be laggy.  But the game will keep migrating to new hosts until it finds a decent one.  The gameplay is properly slow and clunky for a 40k game.  The melee could be better, etc., especially if there were GoW style chainsaw executions.  Most weapons have a pretty slow rate of fire, but do pretty good damage, although the feedback feels a bit off.  

Overall I'm pleasantly surprised with this game.  Maybe I'll finish the campaign eventually just to get the armor set, but I'm shocked to say I'll spent most of my time playing versus.  I've always wanted a decent 40k combat game that wasn't turn based, this game is the closest I've found.  I bought it assuming horde would be my favorite, never imagined that the multiplayer would be so enjoyable.  You can only unlock certain weapon skills in versus, or I might never have tried it.  

SKULLS FOR THE SKULL THRONE is a brilliant Steam event.  This game is definitely worth picking up on sale so you can join in the eternal slaughter.  

FOR THE EMPEROR!

A relatively short third-person shooter that has you playing as Captain Titus of the Space Marines. It knows exactly what it's going for and has adequate mechanics to keep you interested. The frequency of new weapon unlocks and upgrades is good, and gives you new ways to slay orcs with your righteous battle brothers. I'd recommend this if you're a fan of the Warhammer 40k universe (obviously), or if you like other high adrenaline third-person shooters like Vanquish or Binary Domain. Use a controller rather than try to decipher commands like "Mouse 5." I can't speak to multiplayer as the matchmaking is about as slow as you'd expect from a 2011 game.
What can I say about this game... It's not a bad game at all but It's not that type of game I love. Overall it's a good game!
